Each scene should be complete in itself. It should answer: Who & what the scene is about? What is the problem to be solved?  How is the problem solved? What’s next?
A scene moves the story forward. Each scene gets the audience excited about the next scene.
Any unnecessary information is to be avoided while building the scene.
All scenes are about change. When a feeling, action, intention, mood, or people change, the next scene is introduced.
All your words evoke feeling. The story is about emotion. The audience feels with your characters. Make your scenes about feeling.
Use verbs. Avoid too many adjectives. Only use what’s important to understand any of the elements of the outline.
